title: Console: add scaling audit events API (pagination, filtering, retention) + RBAC
author: Chloe Martin
release_notes: Console backend now exposes scaling audit events for Dedicated pools (read-only) with cursor pagination, server-side filtering, retention enforcement, and RBAC checks. Enables Scaling History UI and support workflows.
description:
Context: Dedicated autoscaling now emits structured scaling decision/audit events (bounds clamps, scale up/down, freezes, etc). Console needs a backend API to fetch this history with pagination and filtering, plus strict access controls and a retention policy consistent with telemetry cost constraints. This PR adds read-only endpoints used by the upcoming Console “Scaling History” panel, and aligns the API with ENG-2846 decision log fields (clamp_reason, desired/applied replicas, signal summary) while avoiding high-cardinality/PII leaks. Links: ENG-2847; related: ENG-2846 (metrics) and bounds work (ENG-2843/2845).

What’s included: (1) New Console backend endpoints: GET /console/v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/scaling-audit-events (cursor pagination) and GET /console/v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/scaling-audit-events/{event_id} (details). (2) Server-side filtering: time range (from/to), event_type, clamp_reason, outcome (applied|no_op|rejected), and freeform query on decision_id (exact match) for support triage. (3) Pagination: opaque base64 cursor backed by (occurred_at, event_id) seek pagination; default limit=50, max limit=200. (4) Retention enforcement: events older than retention_days are not returned; default 30 days, configurable per customer tier (Dedicated Enterprise: 90 days) via existing Console config service. (5) RBAC: requires BOTH pool read permission and scaling-audit read permission; denies cross-tenant access and validates pool_id belongs to the customer org. (6) Response shaping: returns a stable summary payload for list view and a separate detail view; detail includes redacted signal snapshot (no raw request IDs, no per-request prompts, no unbounded key/value).

API details: List response returns events sorted newest-first with fields: event_id, occurred_at, pool_id, region, hardware_class, event_type (scale_up|scale_down|clamp|min_floor|max_cap|freeze|unfreeze), desired_replicas, applied_replicas, min_bound, max_bound, clamp_reason (none|min|max|rate_limit|cooldown|fleet_shortage), actor_type (system|user), actor_id (nullable), decision_id, forecast_confidence (nullable), and a short "why" string for UI tooltips. Detail endpoint returns the above plus a structured inputs blob (queue_depth, gpu_util, p95_latency, throttles, forecast_qps, forecast_tokens_per_s) with coarse rounding and fixed keys to avoid cardinality creep.

Storage/queries: Adds a console_read_model table scaling_audit_events (partitioned by occurred_at month; index on (pool_id, occurred_at desc, event_id desc) and (pool_id, decision_id)). The table is populated via the existing internal event bus consumer (console-ingest) which already ingests other ops events; this PR adds the scaling-audit topic handler and applies a schema validator + redaction step before insert.

Security & compliance: Audit endpoints are read-only; responses intentionally omit IPs, user agents, and raw telemetry IDs. Access is logged (who accessed which pool and when) via existing console audit middleware, to satisfy customers asking for “auditability of audit access” during compliance reviews.

Testing: Unit tests cover cursor pagination invariants (no gaps/dupes across pages), filter combinations, RBAC denial cases (wrong org, missing permission, disabled feature), and retention cutoff behavior. Integration tests use a seeded dataset with mixed event types and validate stable ordering under identical timestamps.

Rollout: Gated behind feature flag console.scaling_audit.enabled and allowlist by org. Default off. Once enabled, API is available in all regions but reads from the nearest console read replica; if replica lag is >60s, list endpoint returns a warning header X-Console-Data-Lag-Sec for UI to display a subtle “data may be delayed” note.

Follow-ups: (a) UI wiring (PR-22011) to call these endpoints, (b) export to customer SIEM (separate work; not in scope), (c) add additional filters for “cooldown prevented scale-down” once clamp_reason taxonomy is finalized.

Screenshots: N/A (backend only).

Checklist: - [x] Backward compatible - [x] Feature flagged - [x] RBAC reviewed - [x] Tests added - [x] Observability (request metrics + error logging) - [x] API docs stubbed in console-openapi.
commit_summary: console/rbac: introduce scaling_audit:read permission and enforcement middleware
console/ingest: consume scaling-audit topic, validate schema, redact inputs, store read model
console/db: add scaling_audit_events table + indexes + partitions
console/openapi: add list/detail endpoints and query params
tests: pagination + filtering + retention + RBAC coverage
review_conversation:
Jada Williams: Can we avoid exposing raw signal payloads in the list endpoint? We should keep list payload small and stable for UI performance. Also, please confirm cursor pagination is seek-based (no OFFSET) to prevent page drift.
Chloe Martin (author): Yep—list endpoint is summary only; details endpoint returns the (redacted) inputs blob. Pagination is seek-based using (occurred_at,event_id) with an opaque cursor; no OFFSET. Added tests for stable pagination under duplicate timestamps.

Allison Grant: Retention: please ensure queries enforce retention server-side and that UI cannot request older data by widening the time range. Also consider cardinality—don’t allow arbitrary “inputs” keys through.
Chloe Martin: Enforced retention cutoff in query builder regardless of requested from/to; requesting outside range returns empty. Inputs blob is whitelisted + rounded; any unknown keys dropped at ingest. Added comments and tests.

Rafael Mendes: For oncall, we’ll need decision_id lookup. Can we filter by decision_id exactly? Also please add a warning header for replica lag so UI can communicate delayed events.
Chloe Martin: Added decision_id exact-match filter + index. Added X-Console-Data-Lag-Sec header when replica lag >60s (using existing lag probe).

Marcus Lin: RBAC: make sure this is not just “pool:read”. We need an explicit permission so we can scope access in regulated orgs. Also log access to these endpoints.
Chloe Martin: Added scaling_audit:read permission and require both. Endpoint access is logged via existing console audit middleware (action=scaling_audit.read, resource=pool_id).

Jada Williams: One more nit: query params naming—use occurred_from/occurred_to instead of from/to to avoid collisions with generic middleware.
Chloe Martin: Renamed to occurred_from/occurred_to in OpenAPI + implementation; updated tests.

Approvals: Jada Williams approved. Allison Grant approved. Rafael Mendes approved. Marcus Lin approved.
post_merge_notes: Flag remains OFF by default; enablement tracked via allowlist rollout tooling. Coordinate with PR-22011 (UI) for end-to-end verification in staging before design partner rollout.
